tasks.title: Report the applied ruleset in Hello: LandlockReport proto, ProtocolMinor 2, sandbox.LandlockInfo with Satisfies, agent.Config.Landlock and AgentInfo.Landlock
steps: Write TS-15-21 in sandbox/internal/sandboxpb/landlock_proto_test.go, TS-15-22, TS-15-23 and TS-15-24 in sandbox/landlock_test.go, TS-15-25 in sandbox/internal/agent/landlock_test.go and TS-15-26 in sandbox/internal/attach/landlock_test.go, and confirm they fail

In sandbox/internal/sandboxpb/sandbox.proto add `message LandlockReport { uint32 abi = 1; uint32 kernel_abi = 2; bool tcp = 3; string note = 4; repeated string writable = 5; repeated string read_only = 6; }` and `LandlockReport landlock = 7;` to HelloResponse with a comment that protocol 1.2 added it, renumbering nothing; run `make proto` to regenerate sandbox.pb.go, sandbox_grpc.pb.go and sandbox.proto.sha256, and confirm a second `make proto` leaves no diff

Set ProtocolMinor to 2 in sandbox/version.go with ProtocolMajor unchanged; update TS-14-5 (sandbox/internal/sandboxpb/version_test.go), every other test that pins minor 1 (search the sandbox tree for ProtocolMinor, `1.1` and `protocol 1.1`) and TS-13-24 in sandbox/cmd/agentkit-sandboxd/main_test.go to expect `(protocol 1.2)`

Add sandbox/landlock.go: `type LandlockInfo struct { ABI int; KernelABI int; TCP bool; Note string; Writable []string; ReadOnly []string }` in exactly that field order with a doc comment per field, `const LandlockMinABI = 2` and `const LandlockTCPABI = 4`, and `func (l LandlockInfo) Satisfies(mode NetworkMode) bool` returning `l.ABI >= LandlockMinABI && (mode != NetworkNone || l.TCP)`

Add `Landlock LandlockInfo` to AgentInfo, replacing 13's 'Later scopes add the Landlock ABI there' remark with a doc comment that says it is filled from Hello and carries the protocol note for agents older than 1.2

Add `Landlock sandbox.LandlockInfo` to agent.Config in sandbox/internal/agent/agent.go, documented as data handed in by the caller (the agent package never applies Landlock); in Hello always set HelloResponse.Landlock to a non-nil *sandboxpb.LandlockReport copied field for field from it (int to uint32, slices copied)

In sandbox/internal/attach/attach.go, after the major-version check, fill AgentInfo.Landlock: when the agent's minor is 1 or lower or the report is nil use `LandlockInfo{Note: fmt.Sprintf("agent protocol %d.%d does not report Landlock", major, minor)}`; otherwise convert field for field (uint32 to int), turning an empty repeated field into a nil slice so a round trip deep-equals the agent's input

Extend sandbox/internal/fakeagent with options that set Hello's protocol version and its LandlockReport (e.g. WithHello(major, minor), WithLandlock(report), WithoutLandlock()) and a way to observe that the client closed its connection; the default answers protocol 1.2 with an empty report so existing fakeagent-based tests stay green
Run `go test ./sandbox/... -count=1` and `make lint`

tasks.title: Create sandbox/internal/confine with Plan, the probe seam and the outcome, and promote go-landlock to a direct requirement with its ruling

Verify in the module cache (`go doc github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock/landlock` and `go doc github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock/landlock/syscall`) that Config with V2, V3 and V4, Config.Restrict, Config.RestrictPaths, RODirs, RWDirs, ROFiles, RWFiles, PathAccess with the AccessFS rights, FSRule.WithRefer and syscall.LandlockGetABIVersion exist; if one is missing and cannot be replaced (the probe alone may fall back to syscall.Syscall(444, 0, 0, 1)), write docs/errata/sandbox_landlock_agent.md naming the symbol and version and stop

Write sandbox/internal/confine/plan_test.go (no build constraint) for TS-15-8 and sandbox/internal/confine/outcome_test.go for TS-15-14 and internal/policy/landlock_dep_test.go for TS-15-40, and confirm they fail

Add sandbox/internal/confine/plan.go with no build constraint: `type Decision struct { ABI int; TCP bool; Note string }` and `func Plan(kernelABI int, probeErr error, mode sandbox.NetworkMode) Decision` implementing the decision table with the exact notes (`Landlock unavailable: <error>`, `kernel reports no Landlock support`, the ABI 1 cross-directory-rename note, `kernel Landlock ABI k cannot restrict TCP (needs ABI 4, Linux 6.7)` under none at 2 or 3), capping ABI at sandbox.LandlockTCPABI, TCP only under none at 4, and under allowlist with ABI above 0 a note saying Landlock cannot express a host allowlist and TCP is left to the provider

In an unconstrained file add the unexported seam `var probeABI = kernelProbe` and `func decide(mode sandbox.NetworkMode) (sandbox.LandlockInfo, Decision)` that calls probeABI exactly once and returns KernelABI as the probed value (0 after an error, never capped) with ABI, TCP and Note from Plan

Add sandbox/internal/confine/probe_linux.go with `//go:build linux` defining kernelProbe through go-landlock's syscall.LandlockGetABIVersion, and probe_other.go with `//go:build !linux` defining kernelProbe as an error naming runtime.GOOS; use only the standard syscall package elsewhere so golang.org/x/sys stays indirect

Run `go mod tidy`; confirm go-landlock moves to the direct require block at the unchanged version, kernel.org/pub/linux/libs/security/libcap/psx and golang.org/x/sys stay `// indirect`, and `go list -m all` equals the snapshot; if any version would move, revert, write docs/errata/sandbox_landlock_agent.md and stop

Add github.com/landlock-lsm/go-landlock to approvedDeps in internal/policy/deps_test.go with a one-line reason comment (the sandbox agent's own Landlock confinement), update TS-14-42 to expect it direct and extend TS-13-65's direct-set literal with it

Add the go-landlock ruling to docs/DEPS.md in the existing format (confine directly and rsyncd indirectly, always with DontRestrict(); the version; all-thread application through psx in cgo and non-cgo builds; pulls in psx and x/sys; BestEffort never used because it succeeds silently without Landlock) and a Rejected row for raw Landlock syscalls through x/sys/unix
Run `go test ./sandbox/internal/confine/... ./internal/policy/... -count=1` and `make lint`

tasks.title: Build the ruleset's roots and apply it through Setup with a strict V2–V4 configuration on Linux, with a non-Linux stub
steps: Write TS-15-1, TS-15-4 and TS-15-7 in sandbox/internal/confine/rules_test.go (no build constraint, expectations filtered by what exists on the host), TS-15-2, TS-15-3, TS-15-10 and TS-15-9's child halves in sandbox/internal/confine/setup_linux_test.go, TS-15-9's file checks in plan_test.go and TS-15-13 in stub_test.go (constraint check, every platform) plus setup_other_test.go (`//go:build !linux`); confirm they fail

Move the agent's temporary-directory resolution (TMPDIR of the explicit env, else TEMP, TMP, /tmp) into one helper, sandbox/internal/agentenv.TempDir(env []string) (dir, source string) with source naming the supplying variable, and make the agent's default spill directory use it with no behaviour change

In sandbox/internal/confine/rules.go (no build constraint) define `Inputs{Workdir string; Env []string; RO, RW []string; Mode sandbox.NetworkMode}`, an own access-right bit set mirroring Landlock's filesystem rights with fullFS(abi) (refer from 2, truncate from 3), replaceable package vars systemDirs (/usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /lib32, /lib64, /libx32, /etc, /opt) and deviceFiles (/dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/full, /dev/random, /dev/urandom), and `buildRules(in Inputs, abi int) (plan, error)` returning rules, Writable, ReadOnly and notes

Add rules in this order: writable roots workdir, HOME, temporary directory and each --landlock-rw with fullFS(abi); system dirs and each --landlock-ro with ReadFile|ReadDir|Execute; /proc with ReadFile|ReadDir; device files as file rules with ReadFile|WriteFile plus Truncate at ABI 3 and later (tools/exec.go opens /dev/null and shells open devices with O_TRUNC); Writable lists writable roots then device files, ReadOnly lists system dirs, --landlock-ro paths and /proc

Resolve every root with filepath.EvalSymlinks before adding it and collapse roots resolving to an already-added path; a missing (ENOENT) system or device path is skipped silently, a missing --landlock-ro or --landlock-rw path is skipped with a note naming it, and any other resolution error (e.g. EACCES) is returned as an error naming the path

Skip HOME or the temporary directory with a note naming the supplying variable and the reason when it is unset or empty, relative, missing, resolves to `/`, or resolves to a path equal to or an ancestor of a system directory (compare against both the literal and the resolved system paths)

Add sandbox/internal/confine/setup_linux.go with `//go:build linux`: `func Setup(in Inputs) (sandbox.LandlockInfo, error)` calls decide once; at applied ABI 0 it returns the outcome with nil lists and applies nothing; otherwise it builds the rules, maps them to go-landlock (RWDirs(...).WithRefer() or PathAccess with the exact set, RODirs, PathAccess(ReadFile|ReadDir) for /proc, file rules for devices), picks landlock.V2, V3 or V4 by the applied ABI, calls Restrict when the Decision's TCP is true and RestrictPaths otherwise, never BestEffort, and returns Writable, ReadOnly and the Plan note joined with the skip notes by `; `

Add sandbox/internal/confine/setup_other.go with `//go:build !linux` and no go-landlock import: Setup returns `sandbox.LandlockInfo{Note: "Landlock is Linux-only (GOOS=" + runtime.GOOS + ")"}` and nil

Write a re-exec helper for the Linux tests: the parent runs os.Args[0] with -test.run=^Name$ and an environment marker, the child applies and prints a completion marker, the parent asserts exit 0 and the marker; probe the kernel independently with syscall.Syscall(444, 0, 0, 1) and t.Skipf naming the ABI found

Use only the standard syscall package in tests (PR_GET_NO_NEW_PRIVS = 39 through syscall.SYS_PRCTL, syscall.EACCES) so golang.org/x/sys stays indirect; in TS-15-3 dial through net.Dialer and bind through net.ListenConfig, both with SetMultipathTCP(false), because Landlock's TCP rules do not cover Multipath TCP
Run `go test ./sandbox/internal/confine/... ./sandbox/internal/agent/... -count=1` on Linux, `GOOS=darwin go vet ./sandbox/...` and `make lint`
